_about: Every number and quoted phrase the episode asserts, in both variants. Each node carries `_source` with the quote and the reference; the `ru` / `en` leaves under it are the wording, not separate claims. `panic`, `greenspan`, `capex`, `equities`, `specialist` and `split` are drawn on the frame from here; `book` and `shift` back claims the narrator speaks but that no overlay repeats, and are kept so every assertion has a source in one place. Full references and caveats: sources.md.

panic._source: PBS American Experience, «The Panic of 1873»: «89 of the country's 364 railroads crashed into bankruptcy»; Jay Cooke & Company closed its doors on 18 September 1873. Secondary source; no scholarly citation given for the count.

sourceLine.en: PBS American Experience, The Panic of 1873

book._source: Alan Greenspan, Adrian Wooldridge, «Capitalism in America: A History», Penguin Press, 16 October 2018, ISBN 978-0-7352-2244-1. Russian edition: «Капитализм в Америке. История», Альпина Паблишер.

greenspan._source: Greenspan chaired the Federal Reserve from 11 August 1987 to 31 January 2006 — 18 years and 5 months. Testimony to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, 23 October 2008 (NPR transcript): «I found a flaw. I don't know how significant or permanent it is. But I have been very distressed by that fact.»

capex._source: Yahoo Finance, Myles Udland, 30 April 2026, «'Magnificent 7' earnings rush reveals AI spending surge, with hyperscaler capex set to reach $725 billion in 2026»: «As of Wednesday night's reports, that number is closer to $725 billion» — the big four hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta), against a pre-earnings high-end estimate of about $670 billion. A plan, not spend already booked; later 2026 tallies put the total near $730 billion. The owner's post attributed the figure to Bloomberg; that attribution could not be confirmed (sources.md).

sourceLine.en: Yahoo Finance, 30 Apr 2026, from Q1 earnings — planned, not booked

equities._source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Distributional Financial Accounts, series WFRBST01122 «Share of Corporate Equities and Mutual Fund Shares Held by the Top 1% (99th to 100th Wealth Percentiles)»: 50.9 percent of aggregate, Q2 2026, not seasonally adjusted; page updated 18 September 2026. The Fed notes that hedge fund and private debt fund shares are still counted inside this category in the DFA.

label.en: of US household corporate equities is held by the top 1%

sourceLine.en: Federal Reserve, Distributional Financial Accounts, Q2 2026

specialist._source: Illustrative example, not a measurement: our own restatement of the owner's post («специалиста, который раньше тратил неделю на подготовку исследования, а теперь делает его за день»). No study is claimed.

split._source: Our own wording of the owner's post: «Выгоду получит заказчик, который платит меньше. Что-то достанется работодателю. Часть денег уйдёт поставщику модели. А специалисту вовсе не гарантировано повышение дохода.» A reasoning step, not a measured split.

shift._source: Our own wording of the owner's post: «Человек перестаёт зарабатывать исключительно на собственных рабочих часах и получает возможность владеть продуктом, который приносит доход многократно.» An argument about a possibility, not a forecast.
